summary: Upgraded the ClientApp from Angular 13.4 to Angular 14.3 with `ng update @angular/core@14 @angular/cli@14`, which ran the v14 CLI and core migrations (defaultProject removal, defaultCollection -> schematicCollections, ES2020 compilation target, typed-forms opt-out) and @ngrx/* followed to 14.3.3. No hand-written fixes beyond the migrations were needed: install, build and the SSR build all pass from a clean node_modules. Tests still fail exactly as at baseline, for the same pre-existing reason.
changes: ng update @angular/core@14 @angular/cli@14 bumped all @angular/* packages to 14.3.0 and @angular/cli / @angular-devkit/build-angular to 14.2.13. TypeScript stayed at ~4.6.4, which is within Angular 14's supported range (4.6-4.8), so no bump was needed.

CLI v14 migration removed the deprecated `defaultProject` key from angular.json; the CLI now resolves the project from the working directory, and this workspace has a single project so behaviour is unchanged.

CLI v14 migrations also ran the no-op cleanups for this workspace: `showCircularDependencies` removal, `defaultCollection` -> `schematicCollections`, library secondary-entrypoint package.json removal, and switching the Angular dependency version prefixes to `^`.
CLI v14 migration raised tsconfig.json's compilation target from es2015 to es2020, the new Angular 14 default.

Core v14 typed-forms migration rewrote src/app/add-employee/add-employee.component.ts to use `UntypedFormBuilder` / `UntypedFormGroup` instead of `FormBuilder` / `FormGroup`. This is the official opt-out: the reactive form in the add/edit screen keeps its untyped runtime behaviour instead of picking up v14's new generic typing.
Core v14 `entryComponents` and `pathMatch` migrations found nothing to change in this app.
Ran ng update @ngrx/store@14, moving all five @ngrx/* packages from 13.2.0 to 14.3.3 so their Angular peer range matches v14; the router-store 'road to v14' migration found nothing to change.
Restored the trailing newline on package.json that the ng update rewrite dropped.
package-lock.json regenerated through npm; verified by deleting node_modules and running a plain `npm install` (no --legacy-peer-deps needed), then `npm run build` and `npm run build:ssr`.
manual_followups: `npm run test` still fails exactly as at baseline: angular.json's test target lists "styles.css" instead of "src/styles.css", so the CLI aborts with ENOENT before karma starts. Left untouched to keep this hop to the upgrade; worth fixing on its own.

add-employee.component.ts now uses the Untyped* form classes. That is only an opt-out shim; a person should decide whether to adopt Angular 14's typed reactive forms (FormGroup<{...}>) for the employee form, which would give real type checking on the form value.

`npm run lint` is still broken from the v13 hop: the tslint architect targets were deleted and nothing replaced them. The project should move to @angular-eslint and drop tslint/codelyzer from optionalDependencies.
`relativeLinkResolution: 'legacy'` is still set in src/app/app.module.ts. It is removed in Angular 15, so routerLink resolution must be checked and the option dropped in the next hop.
angular.json still carries `defaultConfiguration: ""` on the build and server targets from the v12 migration. A person should decide whether the default build ought to be production.

The SSR entry (src/main.server.ts) still appears to be dead code: Startup.cs uses UseSpa/UseAngularCliServer and never UseSpaPrerendering. Consider removing the server target and aspnet-prerendering entirely.
node-sass 4.x still fails to build its native binding on Node 16 and is skipped as an optional dependency; it is unused by the build but should be dropped or replaced with `sass`.
core-js is still pinned at ^2.6.5 and @types/node at ^12; both are stale and will need attention in a later hop.
A runtime smoke test of the CRUD screens is worth doing, since the build only proves compilation. The add/edit employee form is the component this hop actually touched.
